title: TikTok Creative Center Guide: Top Ads, Trends and Keywords
summary: How to use TikTok Creative Center for ad research: Top Ads filters, trends, keyword insights, what the metrics mean, and what it will not tell you.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- **TikTok Creative Center** is TikTok's free research site for advertisers. It shows top-performing ads, trending hashtags, sounds, creators and videos, and the keywords used in ad text.
- Use **Top Ads** to see what works in your industry, region and objective. Use **Trends** to choose sounds and hashtags. Use **Keyword Insights** to see the words in winning ad text.
- It is a curated view of what performs, not an archive. It will not list every ad from one competitor.
- You do not need to run ads to use it, and most of it works without a TikTok Ads account.
- For one brand's full list of ads, use an ad library. See the[guide to tracking TikTok competitors](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/track-tiktok-competitors-without-following) .


TikTok rewards fresh creative more than any other platform, and fresh ideas have to come from somewhere. The Creative Center is the cheapest source: a free, official library of what is working right now. Here is how to use each part, and how to turn browsing into a creative brief.


## What the Creative Center is


It is a set of research tools that TikTok publishes for advertisers and creators. Its main sections change over time, and as of now they include:


- **Top Ads:** a gallery of high-performing ads.
- **Trends:** popular hashtags, songs, creators and videos.
- **Keyword insights:** the words and phrases that show up in ad text.
- **Creative tools and inspiration:** TikTok's own creative tools and resources for making ads.


Open the site, pick a region at the top, and start with Top Ads.


## Top Ads


This is the section most advertisers use. It lists ads that performed well, drawn from ads running on TikTok in the region you choose.


### Filters


- **Region.** Ads differ a lot by country. Pick the market you sell in.
- **Industry.** Choose the category closest to yours. Categories can be broad, so scan a neighbor category too.
- **Objective.** Traffic, conversions, app installs, video views and others. A conversion ad and a reach ad win for different reasons.
- **Time period.** A short window shows what is hot now. A long one shows what lasts.
- **Ad format and language.** Narrow to the formats you plan to make.


### What each ad shows


Open an ad to see the video, how long it is, and a set of performance indicators. These are shown as ranked or relative measures, such as likes, shares, and click-through and conversion indicators where the data is available. TikTok does not show actual spend, cost per result or conversion counts. Treat the indicators as a way to compare ads, not as numbers to benchmark yourself against.


You may also see the hook, the first seconds, flagged, and the ad's call to action.


## Trends


Trends lists what is rising on the platform by region and time period.


- **Hashtags.** Popularity and growth. Use them to understand what topics are moving, not to stuff captions.
- **Songs.** Rising sounds. Check licensing before you use one in an ad. A song available for organic posts is not always cleared for commercial use, and Business accounts are limited to the Commercial Music Library. See[what a TikTok Pro account is](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/what-is-a-tiktok-pro-account) .
- **Creators.** Fast-growing accounts. A useful list for finding partners and Spark Ads candidates. See[TikTok Spark Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/tiktok-spark-ads) .
- **Videos.** Breakout posts to study for format and pacing.


Trends age quickly. A trend you see rising this week may be tired in a month, so plan for a short production time.


## Keyword Insights


Keyword Insights shows which words and phrases appear in ad text and how they perform in a category. Use it to:


- Find the language buyers react to, such as "dermatologist recommended" or "free shipping".
- Spot rising phrases early.
- Write on-screen text and captions with the words your market already uses.


The data describes the platform's ads, not your product. A high-performing phrase is a lead, not a rule.


## A 30-minute workflow


1. **Pick one objective and one region.** Mixing them muddies the picture.
2. **Save 10 ads.** Browse Top Ads for your industry. Save the ones you would stop for, not the ones you like most.
3. **Log each ad.** Record the hook (the first two seconds), the format, the length, the sound, the on-screen text, the offer and the call to action.
4. **Count patterns.** If seven of ten open with a talking head and a problem statement, that is the current convention in your category.
5. **Check Trends.** Pick one sound and one hashtag worth using, subject to licensing.
6. **Check Keyword Insights.** Pull five phrases for your captions.
7. **Write three briefs.** Each combines a hook you saw, your own proof and your offer. Do not copy an ad. The method for breaking one apart is in[analyze competitor ads for winning hooks](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/analyze-competitor-ads-winning-hooks) .


## What the Creative Center will not tell you


- **A specific competitor's full ad list.** It shows ads that qualify as top performers, so a brand's average ads are missing.
- **Spend, cost and conversions.** No real numbers, only indicators.
- **Whether the ad works for you.** Different product, price and audience mean different results.
- **Everything in your market.** Smaller regions and niches have thinner data.


To fill the gap, use an ad library. The[TikTok ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/tiktok-ads-library) on Sprites tracks ads brand by brand, with pages such as[Gymshark ads](https://www.sprites.ai/gymshark-ads) ,[Duolingo ads](https://www.sprites.ai/duolingo-ads) and industry pages like[fitness ads](https://www.sprites.ai/fitness-ads) . For ads shown in the EU, TikTok's Commercial Content Library is the official archive.


## Turning research into a test plan


The point of research is to make better tests. Take your three briefs and run them as three ads in one ad group, then keep the winner and rewrite the other two. ## Frequently asked questions


### What is TikTok Creative Center?


It is TikTok's free research site for advertisers. It shows top-performing ads, trending hashtags, songs, creators and videos, and keyword insights for ad text.


### Is TikTok Creative Center free?


Yes. You can browse it without running ads, and most of it works without a TikTok Ads account, though a few features may ask you to sign in.


### Can I see a competitor's ads in Creative Center?


Only if they appear among the top-performing ads. It is not a full archive of one brand's ads. Use an ad library, or TikTok's Commercial Content Library for the EU, for that.


### Does Creative Center show ad spend?


No. It shows performance indicators such as engagement and click or conversion signals, not spend or cost per result.


### Can I use trending sounds from Creative Center in my ads?


Check the licensing first. A sound that is popular for organic posts may not be cleared for commercial use. Business accounts are limited to the Commercial Music Library.


### How often should I check Creative Center?


Weekly is enough for most brands, since trends turn over fast. Check more often when you are planning a launch or a seasonal push.
